title: The Froth That Gives Itself Away
synopsis: A woman with profuse yellow-green discharge and vulvar irritation is diagnosed with trichomoniasis. The classic frothy discharge and strawberry cervix point to the diagnosis, and a single dose of metronidazole cures both her and her partner.

chapters.heading: Scene 1 — With the patient
chapters.body: She shifts uncomfortably on the exam table, her thighs pressed together. The triage nurse takes vitals and notes a low blood pressure of 101/64 and a heart rate of 90, while her temperature sits at 37.9°C. She describes a profuse, frothy, yellow-green discharge that smells foul, and she winces when she mentions the burning with urination.
chapters.visualHint: Medium close-up of the patient sitting on the exam table, legs crossed, face tense with discomfort. Her hands rest on her lower abdomen.

chapters.heading: Scene 2 — With the attending
chapters.body: Dr. Oppong kneels beside the bed and explains that the frothy discharge is a classic sign of trichomoniasis — a protozoan that ferments sugar in the vagina, producing gas as a byproduct. He points out that the cervix has tiny red spots, like a strawberry, which is another hallmark of the infection. The patient nods, relieved to have an explanation.
chapters.visualHint: Wide shot of the attending physician kneeling beside the patient, gesturing toward the exam table. The patient's gown is visible, and the room is softly lit.

chapters.heading: Scene 3 — Orders and data
chapters.body: The attending orders a wet mount and NAAT to confirm the diagnosis, and a single dose of metronidazole 2 grams by mouth. The wet mount shows motile trichomonads swimming under the microscope, and the vaginal pH is 5.0 — higher than the normal 4.5. The whiff test is positive, releasing a fishy odor when potassium hydroxide is added.
chapters.visualHint: Close-up of the microscope eyepiece showing motile trichomonads, with the lab technician adjusting the focus. The slide is labeled with the patient's ID.

chapters.heading: Scene 4 — Results land
chapters.body: The NAAT comes back positive for Trichomonas vaginalis, confirming the diagnosis. The influenza test is negative, and the HIV and RPR screens are non-reactive. The patient is relieved that she doesn't have HIV, but the attending emphasizes that trichomoniasis is a marker for other STIs, so partner testing is essential.
chapters.visualHint: The attending holds a printed lab report, pointing to the positive Trichomonas result. The patient sits on the bed, looking at the paper with a mix of relief and concern.

chapters.heading: Scene 5 — Treatment and mechanism
chapters.body: The metronidazole works by entering the trichomonad and getting reduced inside its anaerobic fermentation pathway. The reduced form slices the protozoan's DNA like scissors through thread — the same energy pathway that makes the froth is what turns the drug on. One dose, and the protozoan's own metabolism destroys it. The attending explains that the partner needs the same treatment to prevent reinfection, which happens in up to 70% of cases if untreated.
chapters.visualHint: Split screen: left side shows a diagram of a trichomonad with DNA strands being cut, right side shows the patient swallowing the single dose of metronidazole with a glass of water.

chapters.heading: Scene 6 — Plan together
chapters.body: The patient agrees to have her partner come in for treatment and testing. The attending writes a prescription for the partner's metronidazole and schedules a follow-up in one week. She leaves the ED with a clear plan: one dose for her, one for him, and no alcohol for 48 hours. The frothy discharge should dry up within a day.
chapters.visualHint: The patient stands at the discharge desk, holding a prescription paper. The attending shakes her hand, and the partner is visible in the background waiting in the hallway.
